lectures.title: Mahatma Gandhi: life, ideas, ashrams and journals

items: **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi:** born 2 Oct 1869, Porbandar. Barrister; legal training → Inner Temple, London.
**Called as / known as:** Mahatma Gandhi → Mahatma.
Newspaper → English + Gujarati + Hindi + Tamil; first issue → June 1903

parts.t: Return to India and later life
items: Resigned from Congress; not a formal Congress member at Independence
**Jawaharlal Nehru** on Gandhi's death: “The light has gone out of our lives”.

parts.t: Associates: C. F. Andrews and the Chhattisgarh tour
items: **C. F. Andrews:** “Deen Bandhu Andrews”; Gandhi gave him this title.
**C. F. Andrews + Gandhi:** lived with Gandhi at Phoenix Farm.
**C. F. Andrews:** accompanied Gandhi to the Round Table Conference.
**C. F. Andrews:** close to Tagore + Gokhale.
**Sundarlal Sharma** (Chhattisgarh): invited Gandhi for the tour.
**Shaukat Ali:** accompanied Gandhi on Gandhi's 1920 Chhattisgarh tour.
Wealth holders should treat wealth as a social trust
**“Hind Swaraj”** (Mahatma Gandhi): his conception of Swaraj.
**Removal of untouchability:** Gandhi's core association in caste and anti-caste movements → Gandhian social reform.
**All India Anti-Untouchability League:** founded by Gandhi.

lectures.title: Gandhi's Satyagrahas: Champaran, Ahmedabad, Kheda and Dandi

items: **Mahatma Gandhi** is associated with: Champaran; NCM; CDM; Quit India.
**Champaran Movement / Satyagraha:** started / led by Mahatma Gandhi, 1917.
**Issue:** indigo cultivation → Tinkathia system; indigo exploitation → Gandhi.
**Teen Kathiya:** forced indigo cultivation on 3/20th of land.
**Illegal taxes:** plantation owners increased taxes and imposed other illegal exactions on peasants.
**Raj Kumar Shukla:** invited Gandhi to Champaran; associated with Champaran Satyagraha.
**Important personalities:** Mahatma Gandhi, Raj Kumar Shukla, Rajendra Prasad, J.B. Kripalani, Mazhar-ul-Haq.
**Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918):** industrial workers → plague bonus / wage dispute.
**Gandhi's method at Ahmedabad (1918):** fast unto death.
**First hunger strike as weapon:** Ahmedabad (direct exam association).
**Ahmedabad result (1918):** workers received 35% bonus; strike → 21 days.
**Ambalal Sarabhai + Anasuya Behn:** important associates at Ahmedabad.
**Kheda Satyagraha (1918):** peasants → crop failure → revenue remission / suspension.
**Land revenue at Kheda:** revenue demanded despite crop failure; farmers sought relief (crop failure → revenue demand → Kheda Satyagraha).
**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:** associated with Gandhi at Kheda.

parts.t: Rowlatt Satyagraha and the Salt Satyagraha
items: **Salt Tax** (British / National Movement): major target of Gandhian protest; Gandhi → Civil Disobedience → Salt.
**Dandi March:** 12 March 1930; violation of Salt Law → Civil Disobedience.
**Gandhi / Dandi:** broke Salt Law through salt-making (Dandi → Salt Law).
**C. Rajagopalachari:** led Vedaranyam Satyagraha; collected salt from sea (Vedaranyam → Salt Law).
**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:** called as / known as Iron Man of India.
**Sardar Patel** is associated with: Bardoli Satyagraha; integration of princely states.
**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:** presided over the Karachi Session, 1931 (Karachi President → Sardar Patel).
**Karachi 1931, key significance:** Fundamental Rights + National Economic Programme.
**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's portfolio in the Interim Government:** Home Affairs + Information & Broadcasting (I&B) + States.

lectures.title: Subhas Chandra Bose and the Indian National Army

items: **Subhas Chandra Bose:** called as / known as Netaji.
**The Indian Struggle:** book by Subhas Chandra Bose.
**The Springing Tiger:** book by Hugh Toye.
**“Give me blood… freedom”:** Subhas Chandra Bose; context → INA.
First Bose presidency; National Planning Committee
Bose re-elected; internal conflict (Bose–Gandhi group conflict) → later resigned (resignation)
**National Planning Committee (1938):** set up under Subhas Bose; Jawaharlal Nehru → Chairman; K.T. Shah → Secretary.
**Forward Bloc:** founder / key personality Subhas Chandra Bose, 1939.
Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon + Major Iwaichi Fujiwara
Formed under his leadership in July 1942
Key organiser; handed over INA command to Subhas Chandra Bose

parts.t: Bose, the Azad Hind Government and the INA trials
items: Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sehgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
**Join Indian Union Movement:** started by Swamy Ramananda Tirtha; launched on August 7, 1947 against the Nizam's declaration of Hyderabad as an independent sovereign state.
**Swamy Ramananda Tirtha:** leader of Join Indian Union Movement; supported Vishalandhra.
**First President of Hyderabad State Congress:** Govinda Rao Nanal.
**The Story of the Integration of the Indian States:** V.P. Menon.

lectures.title: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar: life, movements and writings

items: **B. R. Ambedkar:** called as / known as Modern Manu.
**Core association:** Depressed Classes; political representation; anti-caste struggle. Exam fact: Communal Award → Poona Pact.
**Neo-Buddhist / Dalit Buddhist Movement:** started / led by B. R. Ambedkar, 1956.
**Mook Nayak:** B.R. Ambedkar; journal started in 1920.
**B. R. Ambedkar:** "Caste is not merely division of labour but division of labourers."
**Division of Labourers:** concept of B.R. Ambedkar.

lectures.title: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and the Drafting Committee

items: **Original members** included B.L. Mitter & D.P. Khaitan; replaced by N. Madhava Rau & T.T. Krishnamachari.

lectures.title: The Andhra movement: Mahasabhas and agreements

items: Secretary: Konda Venkatappayya; demanded separate Telugu university; B.N. Sharma opposed separate Andhra state
Creation of a separate Andhra Province (Andhra Rashtram)
To bridge trust deficits between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders
**Third Andhra Mahasabha (1915):** creation of a separate Andhra Province (Andhra Rashtram) with mother tongue as the medium of instruction in secondary schools.
**First session that demanded a separate Telugu University:** First Andhra Mahasabha (1913).

parts.t: Andhra State Movement and linguistic states
items: **Andhra State Movement:** Konda Venkatappaiah → Father of Andhra State Movement.
**Resolution on linguistic reorganisation of states:** introduced by B.N. Sharma, 1918 (Imperial Legislative Council).
**Visalandhra Movement:** Communist Party; initiated by Communists.
**First major ethnic movement leading to state formation / first movement leading to linguistic state formation:** Andhra Movement.
**First person to fast unto death for linguistic state:** Potti Sriramulu.
Nemali Pattabhirama Rao (President); organized by K. Subrahmanyam
Passed resolution opposing separate Andhra state
**Andhra Mahasabha (Hyderabad State):** founded 1930, formed at Medak conference; Suravaram Pratapa Reddy & Burgula Ramakrishna Rao.
**Andhra Jana Sangham** (formed in 1921 under Madapati Hanumantha Rao) was formally restructured and renamed as the Andhra Mahasabha (AMS).
**First Nizam Andhra Mahasabha:** 1930, Jogipet; Suravaram Pratap Reddy presided.
**11th Session (Bhongir split), 1944:** at the historic 11th Bhongir Session presided over by communist leader Ravi Narayana Reddy, the Communist faction took control of the main Andhra Mahasabha.
**Jatiya Andhra Mahasabha:** the separate (Nationalist) body formed by the moderates led by K.V. Ranga Reddy after the 1944 Bhongir split.
**Vishalandhra Mahasabha, 2nd session:** 1954, Hyderabad; Sri K.V. Ranga Reddy presided; Swamy Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Vishalandhra.
Popularly known as agreement before AP formation
AU Act 1925; inaugurated 26 April 1926 at Bezwada / Bezawada (Vijayawada), the first HQ; Bezwada → Waltair; 1st VC: C.R. Reddy
Founded 1954 at Tirupati (Tirupathi) by T. Prakasam; Rayalaseema higher education

lectures.title: Andhra State, Andhra Pradesh and the reorganisation of states

items: **First state formed on linguistic basis / first Linguistic State in India:** Andhra State (1953).
Indian Society #1; AP Geography #1; AP History #1
**Andhra State formed:** Oct 1, 1953 (separated from Madras); the first linguistic state of Andhra.
**High Court of Andhra State:** 5 July 1954, Guntur; Sri Bagh Pact; 1st CJ Koka Subba Rao.
Bezawada Gopala Reddy (serving from 1955 until the state merged to form Andhra Pradesh in 1956)
**Dhar Commission:** 1948; opined creation of linguistic states is a threat to unity.
**States Reorganisation Commission (SRC):** set up on 22 Dec 1953; Kailashnath Wanchoo was not a member.
**First Linguistic Reorganisation Commission / First State Reorganisation Commission:** States Reorganisation Commission (1953).
**First Constitutional Amendment addressing regional imbalance indirectly:** 7th Constitutional Amendment (1956).
**1960, following the Pataskar Commission's decision:** a large part of Tiruttani Taluka of Chittoor district was given to Tamil Nadu.
**In return:** some villages of Tiruvallur Taluka of Tamil Nadu were added to Andhra Pradesh.
**Territorial change involving Tiruttani:** recall Tamil Nadu.
**Separate Telangana Movement (1969):** formed by Telangana Praja Samithi (TPS) led by Marri Chenna Reddy; CM: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy.
**Marri Chenna Reddy:** President of Telangana Praja Samithi.
**Jai Andhra Movement:** led by Coastal Andhra & Rayalaseema leaders (Kakani Venkataratnam, B.V. Subba Reddy, Tenneti Viswanatham); CM: P.V. Narasimha Rao.
**Trigger of Jai Andhra Movement:** Supreme Court judgement on Mulki rules.
